beats.role_note: The mechanism before the build — the MGMT fork
beats.narration_text: Temozolomide alkylates DNA. Whether that alkylation kills a tumour cell depends entirely on one thing: whether MGMT is available to repair it. This plate shows the fork — repair happens if MGMT is active; the damage persists and kills the cell if MGMT's promoter is methylated.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — fork diagram: VERM lesion strand → upper path (GREEN MGMT enzyme) → SKY intact cell; lower path (BLUE methylated promoter, no MGMT) → VERM break → ORANGE dead cell

beats.role_note: Stakes before the build — glioblastoma, TMZ response, methylation biomarker
beats.narration_text: In glioblastoma, MGMT promoter methylation predicts whether temozolomide will work. Methylated promoter — MGMT silenced — the DNA damage accumulates, the cell dies, and the patient responds. Unmethylated — MGMT active — the damage is repaired, the drug has no effect. Silencing the repair gene is what makes the poison work.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — stat card: MGMT promoter methylated → TMZ works; unmethylated → TMZ repaired away; clinical implication: methylation = chemo sensitivity

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — the REAL Claude Code prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The ask,'
beats.narration_text: The ask. Into Claude: port the mgmt-methylation-paradox plate from plates underscore gen dot py p19 into Manim. A VERM diamond lesion on a GRAY strand. The strand forks two ways. Upper track: GRAY strand, a GREEN pac-arc enzyme at the lesion position, diamond fades out — repaired — then clean GRAY strand, then a SKY intact cell circle. Lower track: a BLUE promoter rectangle, four lollipop methylation marks below it, GRAY strand with the VERM diamond still present, a VERM break mark, then an ORANGE fragmented dead cell polygon. Animate both tracks simultaneously.

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL B05_MgmtMethylation class, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it. The fork is a single GRAY strand at y=0 with a VERM diamond at left-centre; two thin lines diverge upward and downward from a fork point. Upper track at y plus one point eight — four objects: a GRAY left segment, a GREEN arc approximating the pac-man enzyme mouth, a GRAY clean right segment, and a SKY cell circle. Lower track at y minus one point eight — five objects: a BLUE promoter rect, four lollipop marks built as Line plus Dot pairs, a GRAY strand with the VERM diamond persisting, a VERM diagonal break mark, and an ORANGE polygon assembled from six points. The choreography runs both tracks simultaneously after the fork arrows grow: FadeIn upper and lower in parallel, then the enzyme arc moves along the strand as the diamond FadeOuts, while the lower lesion stays put and the break appears. The dead cell is the last object in.

props.title: scenes.py — B05_MgmtMethylation
props.code:
# scenes.py — Claude Code output
SKY="#56B4E9"; BLUE="#0072B2"; GREEN="#009E73"
VERM="#D55E00"; ORANGE="#E69F00"; GRAY="#7c7c7c"

class B05_MgmtMethylation(Scene):
  def construct(self):
    # Lesion strand + VERM diamond
    strand=Line([-6,0,0],[0,0,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=6)
    diamond=Polygon([-3,0.3,0],[-2.5,0,0],[-3,-0.3,0],[-3.5,0,0],
      color=VERM,fill_color=VERM,fill_opacity=0.85,stroke_width=2)
    self.play(FadeIn(strand),FadeIn(diamond),run_time=0.5)
    # Fork
    fk_up=Line([0,0,0],[1,1.8,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.8)
    fk_dn=Line([0,0,0],[1,-1.8,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=1.8)
    self.play(GrowFromPoint(fk_up,[0,0,0]),
              GrowFromPoint(fk_dn,[0,0,0]),run_time=0.55)
    # Upper track
    us=Line([1,1.8,0],[3,1.8,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=5)
    enzyme=Arc(radius=0.35,start_angle=PI*0.18,angle=PI*1.64,
      color=GREEN,stroke_width=5).move_to([2,1.8,0])
    uc=Line([3.4,1.8,0],[5,1.8,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=5)
    cell=Circle(radius=0.5,color=SKY,fill_color=SKY,
      fill_opacity=0.28,stroke_width=3).move_to([6,1.8,0])
    # Lower track
    promo=RoundedRectangle(width=1.8,height=0.6,corner_radius=0.1,
      color=BLUE,fill_color=BLUE,fill_opacity=0.16,stroke_width=2.6
      ).move_to([1.9,-1.8,0])
    lollipops=VGroup(*[VGroup(
      Line([1.1+k*0.4,-1.5,0],[1.1+k*0.4,-1.2,0],color=BLUE,stroke_width=2.4),
      Dot(radius=0.09,color=BLUE).move_to([1.1+k*0.4,-1.15,0])
    ) for k in range(4)])
    ls=Line([3.1,-1.8,0],[5,-1.8,0],color=GRAY,stroke_width=5)
    d2=Polygon([-3+6.5,0.3-1.8,0],[-2.5+6.5,0-1.8,0],
      [-3+6.5,-0.3-1.8,0],[-3.5+6.5,0-1.8,0],
      color=VERM,fill_color=VERM,fill_opacity=0.85,stroke_width=2)
    brk=VGroup(
      Line([5.2,-1.65,0],[5.65,-2.0,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=4),
      Line([5.5,-1.65,0],[5.95,-2.0,0],color=VERM,stroke_width=4))
    dead=Polygon([5.8,-1.3,0],[6.25,-1.6,0],[6.05,-1.9,0],
      [6.35,-2.1,0],[6.1,-2.1,0],[5.9,-1.85,0],
      color=ORANGE,fill_color=ORANGE,fill_opacity=0.5,stroke_width=2.4
      ).move_to([6.2,-1.8,0])
    # Animate
    self.play(FadeIn(us),Create(enzyme),FadeIn(promo),
              LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(l) for l in lollipops],lag_ratio=0.2),
              run_time=0.9)
    self.play(diamond.animate.set_opacity(0),
              enzyme.animate.move_to([3,1.8,0]),
              FadeIn(ls),FadeIn(d2),run_time=0.8)
    self.play(FadeIn(uc),FadeIn(cell),FadeIn(brk),run_time=0.5)
    self.play(FadeIn(dead),run_time=0.4); self.wait(0.8)

beats.role_note: Manim render of B05_MgmtMethylation — fork, both tracks, enzyme repair vs methylated block
beats.narration_text: Run it. The VERM diamond appears on the lesion strand. The fork grows — two thin lines diverging up and down. Upper track: the GREEN enzyme arc appears at the lesion, then moves along the strand as the diamond fades. Clean strand, then a SKY cell circle — the cell survived. Lower track simultaneously: BLUE promoter rect, four lollipop methylation marks, lower strand with the diamond persisting. Then the VERM break mark. Then the ORANGE dead cell polygon. Same damage, two fates.

beats.role_note: ClaudeComposerAsk — revision prompt. SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting = 'The change,'
beats.narration_text: The change. Revise: the enzyme should move along the upper strand — animate its position — and the diamond should FadeOut as the enzyme passes over it, so the repair feels physical. On the lower track, the methylation lollipops should grow from the dots upward — LaggedStart on each one. The VERM diamond on the lower strand should pulse to show it persists. And the dead cell should assemble from polygon fragments — LaggedStart creating each piece.

props.command:
claude "Revise: enzyme moves along the upper strand (animate position), diamond
FadeOut as it passes (repaired). Lower methylation marks grow from dots upward
(LaggedStart). VERM lesion pulses on lower strand (persists). Dead cell
assembles from polygon fragments (LaggedStart Create each piece)."

beats.act: OUTPUT — revised animation with enzyme sweep and fragment assembly
beats.role_note: Manim render of B07_MgmtMethylationFork — enzyme sweeps, lollipops grow, lesion pulses, dead cell assembles
beats.narration_text: Watch the revision. The lesion flashes VERM — emphasis on the damage. The fork grows. Upper: the enzyme arc moves across the strand — you watch it sweep — and the diamond fades out exactly as it passes. The repair is visible as motion. Lower: the lollipop stems grow upward from the dots, one after another — methylation marks installing themselves. The VERM diamond pulses, still there. Break mark appears, and then the dead cell assembles piece by piece. The paradox rendered: the silence of a repair gene is what makes the chemotherapy lethal.

beats.role_note: What we built and what the motion taught
beats.narration_text: The paradox: silencing a DNA repair gene makes chemotherapy work better. The fork animation showed why — same lesion, opposite fate depending on whether the repair crew showed up.
beats.visual_intent: Slate — summary card: MGMT methylated = TMZ works; MGMT active = TMZ fails; 'silencing repair enables killing'; fork = one lesion, two fates

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud AND discussed. greeting = 'Your turn.'
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take this prompt into Claude: extend the fork — add a third branch off the lower track showing what happens when a resistant glioblastoma cell upregulates MGMT despite methylation. Show the lollipop marks fading, the enzyme reappearing on the lower track, and the cell surviving. Why run it? Because acquired chemotherapy resistance in glioblastoma often involves exactly this: re-expression of MGMT even in promoter-methylated tumours. The three-branch fork gives you the full clinical picture — initial sensitivity, then resistance — in one animation. That is the difference between a one-time explainer and a mechanistic model you can actually reason from.

props.command:
claude "Add a third branch: resistant cell on the lower track — lollipop marks
fade (methylation lost), MGMT enzyme reappears, lesion repaired, cell survives.
Show the sequence: initial sensitivity → acquired resistance → survival."
